desc:
Your users already tell you what to build, but the messages sit in different places. Ecom Swift LLC provides a user feedback review and priority plan: we read your tickets, reviews and survey answers and turn them into a ranked list of what to fix and build.

## What is a user feedback review?

A user feedback review is a structured reading of everything your customers have told you: support tickets, app store reviews, survey answers, sales call notes, chat transcripts and emails. The goal is to find patterns, group them into themes and show how often each theme appears.

The result is a plan, not a pile of quotes. Each theme comes with its weight, the real words behind it and a view on how hard it would be to address.

## Why feedback needs sorting

Raw feedback is misleading. The loudest customer seems to represent everyone, and a recent complaint feels bigger than an old one that appeared many times. Teams then build for the last conversation instead of the pattern.

Feedback is also scattered. Support sees one picture, sales sees another and the reviews page shows a third. Nobody has read all of it together, so the same problem can be known in three places and fixed in none.

## How a feedback plan improves product decisions

Ranking by frequency and effect tells you where small work removes the most pain. A theme that comes up often and takes a day to fix is a quick win. A theme that comes up rarely but blocks sign-up may still deserve attention. Seeing both on one page helps your team agree without a long debate.

Real quotes make the case. When you tell a developer or an investor that a theme matters, a handful of customer sentences carry more weight than an opinion. They also keep the team in touch with how users describe their own problems, which improves your copy, help pages and onboarding.

## What a useful feedback review contains

- Every feedback item read, not sampled from the top.
- Themes with clear names, such as sign-up confusion or export problems.
- A count for each theme, so frequency is visible.
- Sample quotes for each theme, with identifying details removed.
- A rating of impact on users and effort to address.
- A short list of quick wins.
- A note on feedback that conflicts, such as users asking for opposite things.
- A list of what users like, so you protect it.
- A draft of next quarter's roadmap, in the larger package.
- A tagging scheme for new feedback, so the work stays easy to repeat.

## How we work

You send us the feedback in whatever format you have: exports from a help desk, spreadsheets, copied reviews or notes. We read it all, build the theme list and refine it until each item sits in the right place. Then we count, rate and rank, and write the plan.

The Basic package covers a set of feedback items with themes, counts and a one-page summary. Standard reads more items, ranks themes by impact and effort, lists quick wins, adds sample quotes and includes a review call. Premium covers the largest set, adds effort estimates, a draft roadmap, a tagging scheme, a short process guide for collecting feedback and a call with your team.

We do not contact your users. We work only with what you already have, and we do not decide what you build: we give your team the evidence to decide.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Send feedback from every channel, including negative and neutral.
- Include dates and customer type when you have them.
- Tell us your main business goal for the quarter.
- Mark which feedback came from key accounts.
- Share the plan with support, sales and product together.

**Avoid:**
- Sending only the best or worst messages.
- Removing context to make files smaller.
- Treating one strong opinion as a trend.
- Building straight from the list without checking effort.
- Collecting feedback and never reading it again.

## Who this is for

This suits a founder with hundreds of support tickets and no time to read them. It suits a product team whose app store reviews are piling up. It also suits a company that wants evidence before choosing the next big feature.

## What we need from you

An export or copy of your feedback in any readable format, a note on your product and its main customer types, and the goal you are planning around. If you want results shared in your tracker, a team user invitation helps. We never need passwords, and we handle customer details as private.
